title: Rainfall Totals Map: Any Dates, Any Point
description: Explore modelled total precipitation for selected dates from the Open-Meteo archive, including snow water equivalent.

quick_answer: This tool sums complete daily precipitation values at 25 sample points from the Open-Meteo archive. Precipitation includes frozen precipitation as water equivalent; it is not a rainfall-only measurement or a gauge record.

faq: Precipitation or rainfall — same thing here?
No. The requested precipitation total includes frozen precipitation as water equivalent; it is not rainfall-only.
How far back can I query?
Coverage varies with the Open-Meteo archive and requested location. Requests with unavailable or incomplete daily data are rejected.
Why does the official gauge disagree with my cell?

A gauge is a point; a cell is an area average over roughly 25–30 km of model grid. A storm that parked over the gauge can triple its reading against the cell — both are honest, about different things.
Can I compare this year with the climate normal?
You can run periods separately, but this tool does not calculate climate normals or anomalies. Use an authoritative climate dataset for those comparisons.
Does it work for monsoon or Mediterranean climates?
Worldwide — the archive is global. Date-ranged queries are exactly how strongly seasonal climates should be read: wet season and dry season separately, never as one misleading annual blur.
What about snowfall in the total?
Use the Snowfall Totals Map for the frozen archive view; this map's precipitation includes melted-water equivalents in the source data, which is rain-gauge language, not snow-depth language.
Can I use this for a water-rights or insurance claim?
No — claims and rights run on official gauge networks and certified records. This is a research and context tool with honest sourcing, which is a different job.
